messages:
tasha: FYI I hit a nasty onboarding surprise: our local quick-runner kept authenticating with an old token after I rotated the canonical secret in GitHub.

ben: Which env names were set?

tasha: The deploy had REDWOOD_API_KEY and RW_KEY both set. Ops rotated REDWOOD_API_KEY only, but the running container still had RW_KEY at process start so it kept using that one.

omar: Classic mixed-legacy state. Do we have a rule anywhere for env precedence?

ryan: Not a single canonical doc. Different SDK releases handled fallbacks differently (some preferred RW_KEY, some REDWOOD_API_KEY). That makes rotation non-atomic unless you also update legacy names.

ben: Repro steps I ran locally: 
```bash
export RW_KEY=oldtok
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newtok
./demo-server &
# server picks RW_KEY until restarted
```

ben: The quick-runner uses an init-time client and doesn't re-read envs on SIGHUP, so secret rotate jobs that only swap REDWOOD_API_KEY won't fix running processes.

tasha: Two issues surfaced: 1) env-name precedence is inconsistent across SDKs, 2) demo apps don't reliably reload credentials.

ryan: Short-term mitigation: update the rotate-key helper in infra templates to write all recognized env names (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_KEY, RW_PROJECT_KEY, RW_ORG_KEY) so rotation is idempotent for pinned SDKs. Also add a note to the helper: "if you vendor an old SDK, rotate legacy env names too."

omar: Agreed. Also for sample apps we should add a minimal SIGHUP handler that re-initializes the client so the container picks up rotated secrets without a full restart.

rotations-bot: Created issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-templates/issues/300, https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-apps/issues/121 labels: rotation, sdk, docs

ben: Medium-term: SDK change - emit a one-line deprecation warn when a legacy env is present and prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY as canonical. That gives visibility in logs when a legacy secret is shadowing the canonical one.

omar: And we need an SDK parity RFC so js/py/go agree on a single precedence order. Breaking behavioral changes are scary, but documenting/locking the canonical precedence avoids these surprises.

ryan: Another important runtime edgecase: streaming clients. Some clients re-auth per-chunk, some only at handshake. If a token rotates mid-stream, servers that accept per-chunk auth may silently accept the old token while others will drop and reconnect. We need a recommendation: prefer handshake auth, and on auth failure return 401 and close the stream so clients reconnect with new creds. Document retry/backoff guidance.

tasha: Could we also add an e2e in demo CI: rotate-key, then run a quick request to the service and assert 200 after a restart (or SIGHUP)? That would catch pinned-sdk situations.

ben: Yes. I'll open the infra PR to: a) update rotate helper to dual-write envs, b) add GH Action snippet in onboarding documenting secret hygiene, c) add e2e job.

omar: I'll open SDK PRs to add the deprecation warning and link to a migration doc. Also add a tiny compat shim that logs once per process if legacy envs present.

ryan: For docs: onboarding "CI secret hygiene" should recommend one secret only (REDWOOD_API_KEY), show how to rotate in GH Actions/GitLab, and include a checklist: remove legacy envs, restart or SIGHUP containers, run smoke test.

rotations-bot: Linked issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/610, https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/412

ben: Plan summary: 1) emergency rotate-helper patch to write all known env names (merge today), 2) demo apps: add SIGHUP reload + e2e, 3) SDKs: deprecation warning + compat shim, 4) RFC for env precedence across languages + runtime note for streaming auth behavior.

tasha: Thanks — this would've been a painful customer incident. Good to patch the helper and add the docs. :heart:
